# PLT: Parallel Loop Transformer for Efficient Test-Time Computation Scaling

English · [简体中文](../zh/2510.24824.md) · [Back to the list](../../README.md)

<sub>arXiv 2510.24824 · 2025-10-28 · ByteDance Seed</sub>

<img src="../../assets/glyphs/2510.24824.svg" alt="[all layers, every loop (100% of layers)] x 2 or 3 (PLT-2 / PLT-3); injection additive; KV first-pass">

> Run loop l of token i in the same forward pass as loop l+1 of token i-1, let later loops reuse the first loop's KV plus a gated SWA, and a looped model decodes at close to unlooped latency and KV.

**Category**: Systems and inference · **Status**: draft (numbers not yet re-checked) · **Impact**: cites 37 · HF upvotes 18 · HN points 3

[paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.24824)

## Problem

In a vanilla looped Transformer the loops run one after another, so per-token compute, decoding latency and KV cache all grow linearly with the number of loops.

## Method

- Cross-loop parallelism (CLP) shifts the previous loop's last-layer states right by one token and adds the embeddings before each non-first loop, so loop l of token i, loop l+1 of token i-1 and so on are decoded as one micro-batch in a single forward pass.
- Non-first loops keep their own queries but attend globally to the first loop's KV, so only one global KV cache is stored.
- Gated SWA (G-SWA) lets non-first loops also attend to their own KV within a 64-token window and mixes local and global outputs through a head-wise sigmoid gate; these loops cache only the most recent w KV entries.

## Loop layout

| Facet | Value |
|---|---|
| Where the loop sits | shifted / parallel across tokens |
| Weight sharing | fully tied |
| Passes in training | fixed |
| Passes at test time | fixed |
| Input injection | additive |
| KV cache | first-pass KV shared |
| Gradient through passes | n/a |
| Origin | trained from scratch |
| FFN | MoE |
| Attention in the loop | hybrid (full + window / linear) |
| Passes (all layers, every loop) | train 2 or 3 (PLT-2 / PLT-3); test 2 or 3, same as training |

Each loop runs the whole stack with tied weights. Before every non-first loop, the previous loop's last-layer states are shifted right by one token and added to the token embeddings, so at decoding time loop l of token i runs in the same forward pass as loop l+1 of token i-1. Non-first loops attend globally to the first loop's KV and locally to their own KV through SWA (w=64), mixed by a head-wise sigmoid gate. The in-house Seed-MoE layer count is not disclosed; the open-source OLMo/OLMoE runs use 16 layers (Appendix A.2.1).

## Other findings

- Adding CLP to the two-loop model leaves average accuracy nearly unchanged (39.7 to 39.6) and cuts decoding latency from 9.4 ms to 5.9 ms, while the KV cache stays at 560M. (Table 2; Section 3.1.2)
- Sharing the first loop's KV halves the KV cache (560M to 280M) but lowers average accuracy from 39.6 to 36.2; adding G-SWA with a 64-token window brings it back to 39.7 at 284M. (Table 2; Section 3.1.2)
- With the same parameters, three loops beat two, with average accuracy 40.8 for PLT-3 against 39.7 for PLT-2; Table 2 lists 5.0 vs 4.9 ms latency and 287M vs 284M KV. (Table 2; Section 3.1.2)
- At batch sizes 32 and 64, PLT-2 cuts per-token decoding latency by 47% relative to the vanilla two-loop model and runs at 1.06× and 1.04× the latency of the unlooped model. (Table 3; Section 3.1.3)
- A PLT-2 with two-thirds of the baseline's layers (1.7B/40B) averages 62.6 against 62.1 for the 2.5B/60B Seed-MoE, with about 30% lower decoding latency. (Table 4; Section 3.2; Figure 5)

## Comparison

- **Baseline**: Unlooped in-house Seed-MoE 680M/13B and the same model looped twice without CLP; CLP, KV sharing and G-SWA are then added one at a time.
- **Held fixed**: N (unique parameters), A (active parameters), D (training tokens)
- **Differs**: F (training FLOPs), L (executed layers per token), KV (KV cache per token)
- **Baseline hyperparameters**: not stated
- **Headline claim**: On a 680M/13B MoE trained on 150B tokens, PLT-2 reaches the vanilla two-loop model's average accuracy of 39.7 (34.7 without loops) at 4.9 ms decoding latency and 284M KV cache (batch size 4), against 9.4 ms and 560M for the vanilla two-loop model and 4.8 ms and 280M for the unlooped model. (Table 2; Section 3.1.2)

## Caveats

- The main results use in-house Seed-MoE models whose data and other training details are withheld; the open-source OLMo/OLMoE runs (1.2B dense and 1B/7B MoE at 400B tokens, plus a 100B-token dense ablation) test only L=2.
- Each model is trained and evaluated at one fixed loop count (L=2 or 3); the paper does not report running a different number of loops at inference.
- Parameters and training tokens are matched but compute is not; an L-loop PLT spends L times the per-token compute of the baseline (Table 1), and its latency advantage rests on decoding being memory-bound.
- CLP parallelizes decoding only; training stays serial along the loop dimension (Figure 4).
- Latency is per-token decoding latency on one GPU with FP8 attention, W4A8 linear layers and a 5000-token prefill; the latency and KV columns of Table 2 are at batch size 4.
- Hyperparameters of the in-house runs are not given, so the paper does not say whether the baseline was tuned separately.
